name: Motion for a resolution
title: MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on Audiovisual Media Services Directive obligations in the transatlantic dialogue
part_text:
The European Parliament is asking the European Commission and member states to defend the EU's audiovisual media rules against US criticism. These rules require streaming services to offer at least 30% European works and let countries make foreign providers pay towards European production. The United States has called these rules a trade barrier. The Parliament says they are fair, apply to everyone equally, and protect European culture. It wants them kept out of trade deals and defended in talks with the US.

- The Parliament asks the Commission to reject US claims that these rules distort trade.
- It affects streaming services and broadcasters in the EU, including US companies.
- Next, the Commission must defend the rules in US trade talks and a 2026 review.
